story.headline: Big 12 says replay officials wrongly awarded BYU a touchdown in its win over Arizona State
story.summary: After No. 8 BYU beat Arizona State 27-20 in Provo, Utah, on Oct. 31, the Big 12 Conference said in a statement that replay officials should not have awarded a first-quarter touchdown. Running back Sione Moa had picked up a fumble by quarterback Bear Bachmeier near the goal line and was credited with a 1-yard score. The conference said the correct ruling was BYU ball, third and goal from the 2.

quote.text: Replay was incorrect in awarding a score. The correct ruling should have been BYU ball for a third and goal attempt from the two-yard line.

story.subject: official-or-institution

sources.title: Big 12: Replay officials erred in awarding BYU touchdown vs. ASU

story.headline: Monroe County, Mich., mistakenly sends a shelter-in-place alert during a drill at the Fermi 2 nuclear plant
story.summary: On the morning of Thursday, Nov. 5, some people subscribed to Monroe County's opt-in Everidge alert system got an emergency message about the Fermi 2 nuclear power plant. County agencies were running a drill at the plant when a shelter-in-place message went out by mistake. It was retracted within minutes, and Michigan State Police said there was no emergency.

quote.text: Monroe County agencies were executing a drill exercise this morning at Fermi II in Frenchtown. An accidental message was sent in ERROR to shelter in place.

story.headline: Uncounted memory card in Seminole County, Ga., flips the lead in a state House race
story.summary: Georgia's secretary of state's office said a post-election check found about 388 more voters checked in at Seminole County polling places on Election Day than ballots reported. After the state notified them, county election officials found a memory card that had not been uploaded. Once those votes were added to the unofficial count, Republican Rep. Gerald Greene went from trailing Democrat Harry James by 58 votes to leading by 262 in House District 154, and Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger opened an investigation.

quote.text: When the secretary of state's office notified county officials about the difference, authorities with the Seminole County Board of Elections discovered that a memory card had not been uploaded to its election management system.
